messages.subject: Problem using the imported outline
parts:
Dear users of geomorph,

I have a problem using the outline I have imported. I followed the workflow of the quick guide with the exception that I could not draw with the "outline mode" of TPSdig, so I drew a curve with "draw curves" mode. I obtained the outline attached as a image. However It doesn't work with visualization functions such as plotRefToTarget. I think the problem is that it does not recognize as an outline.

gpa_mand <- gpagen(mand, curves= NULL)
1. calculate mean shape: 
ref <- mshape(gpa_mand$coords)
2. Choose a specimen
findMeanSpec(gpa_mand$coords)
#13_66598m
#173
3. Read coordinate data of choosed specimen
sp_66598 <- mand[ , ,"13_66598m"]

4. run function to create mean shape outline
av.outline <- warpRefOutline("66598_curves.csv", sp_66598, ref)# I also tried to run this function with the curve of the template as .TPS but return a error

Any help will be greatly appreciated

Julio

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Problem using the imported outline
parts:
Julio,

 

The problem is in your use of warpRefOutline.  You did not follow my advice in the previous email.

 

This function is to be used with reading in an outline of a particular specimen, matching it to the landmarks of that specimen, and then warping it to the reference. What you have done in your code is match it to a ‘findspec’ specimen: that is not correct. 

 

Whichever specimen in your dataset you digitized the outline from, that is what you must use. Otherwise, the outline will be in different scale relative to the data, and will not appear in the TPS or vector deformation plots from plotRefToTarget.

Dean

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Problem using the imported outline
parts:
Julio,

 

I don’t know how I can be more clear. Ignore the help guide. The current maintainers of geomorph do not maintain that guide: it is out of date and does not keep up with the software and frankly, is not our guide!

 

As I mentioned in my previous email, warpRefOutline works best when you provide it the outline of a specimen, point it to the specimen from which you digitized the outline, and then to the reference. You are pointing it to the output of ‘findMeanSpec’, which is not the same thing, and is not guaranteed to work correctly. In none of my previous email responses did I recommend this; because this procedure is not guaranteed to work.

 

I strongly suggest you go back to my responses in this thread and follow the explicit instructions I have provided. If these do not work, we can proceed off-line. But if you do not follow my instructions, it is simply not useful for me (or the geomorph team) to continue to answer your questions.

Dean
